# Jubilees Chapter 29 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob's departure from Laban; wrestling at Peniel

---

**29:1** In the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Jacob went to Laban to take his leave and return to his father in the land of Canaan.

**29:2** Laban called together all his flocks, all his sons, and all his daughters, and embraced and kissed Jacob and wept bitterly. He said to Jacob: "Please do not leave me. You have found favor in my sight. Stay with me, and God will bless me for your sake."

**29:3** But Jacob refused to stay. He said to Laban: "Let me go; my father and my mother are waiting for me. Release me so I may go."

**29:4** Laban took his leave of him with weeping, and Jacob went on his way.

**29:5** Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir.

**29:6** They returned to Jacob with the report: "We went to your brother Esau, and he is coming to meet you with four hundred men."

**29:7** Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed. He divided the people with him and the flocks and herds and camels into two groups,

**29:8** Thinking: "If Esau comes and attacks one group, the remaining group will be able to escape."

**29:9** Jacob prayed to the LORD his God: "O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O LORD, who said to me: 'Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will deal well with you' —

**29:10** I am unworthy of all the steadfast love and faithfulness you have shown your servant, for with only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.

**29:11** Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid of him — afraid that he will come and kill us all, mothers and children together.

**29:12** Yet you said: 'I will surely do you good and make your descendants as the sand of the sea, which is too many to count.'"

**29:13** Jacob stayed there that night and selected a gift for his brother Esau from what he had with him: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams, thirty milking camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

**29:14** He arranged these in separate herds and put them in the care of his servants, with intervals between them.

**29:15** He instructed the lead servant: "When my brother Esau meets you and asks, 'To whom do you belong? Where are you going? And whose animals are these ahead of you?' —

**29:16** Say: 'They belong to your servant Jacob; they are a gift sent to my lord Esau. Jacob himself is also coming behind us.'"

**29:17** Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of day.

**29:18** When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob's hip, and Jacob's hip socket was dislocated as they wrestled.

**29:19** The man said: "Let me go, for the day is breaking." Jacob said: "I will not let you go unless you bless me."

**29:20** The man said: "What is your name?" He said: "Jacob." He said: "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel; for you have striven with God and with men, and you have prevailed."

**29:21** Jacob asked: "Tell me your name, I pray." He said: "Why do you ask my name?" And he blessed him there.

**29:22** Jacob named the place Peniel, saying: "I have seen God face to face, and yet I am alive."

**29:23** The sun rose on him as he crossed over Penuel, limping because of his hip.

**29:24** Therefore to this day the people of Israel do not eat the sinew of the hip that is at the socket of the hip.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal rendering. Jubilees treats the wrestling at Peniel more briefly than Genesis 32, though the essential elements are preserved. The prayer (vv.9-12) is an important theological passage in the Ge'ez, closely following Genesis 32:9-12. The sinew prohibition (v.24) grounds the dietary law in narrative.*
